content.text:
Build the first app-triggered skill for the JusPrin project chat: "a model is opened or imported". Branch from local `jusprin-newui` (tip 46ee617812 or later; 17 commits ahead of origin, do not push). Report, untracked at your worktree root as `skill-model-arrived-report.md`, four parts (problem, what changed, tests and results, remaining issues), plain English for someone who did not see this. Never commit the report. Commit code and tests on your branch with plain messages, no attribution lines; do not merge into `jusprin-newui`, the main session does that.

## The design you are implementing

Kenneth's rule for the project chat: the standing system prompt carries principles only, and everything situational arrives as a skill, a short text the app adds to one request when it knows the situation holds. The app chooses the skill by event; the model never picks one from an index and there is no tool to read one. Four skills are planned; this is the first and it also builds the loading mechanism the other three will reuse: (1) a model is opened or imported; (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully; (3) OrcaSlicer reported a print issue, including the canvas buttons "Explain this issue and my options." and "Help fix this issue."; (4) the project setup changed after a purpose was recorded.

## What exists today

- The skill text: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/fileReportInstructions.ts`, about 6.8 KB. The page sends it once per connection as the bridge message `file_report_instructions` (`App.tsx` line 197; `Protocol::kFileReportInstructions` in `Agent/AgentProtocol.hpp`); the host keeps it in `m_file_report_instructions` (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp`).
- When it fires: only when the person opens or drops a file. `AgentHost::on_file_loaded` (about line 1318) appends a Note message carrying the load report and starts a turn; `make_agent_request` (about lines 2060 and 2112) sends the report as the user text and adds the skill as a developer item on that request only, and a one-line reminder on later requests (line 2115). A project reopened with an existing conversation and no OrcaSlicer messages is skipped on purpose.
- What does not fire it: `project_open` and `object_import_file` run by a tool. Their replies carry the same load report (`Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` about lines 1050 to 1105, `load_report_result`) but no skill. The model then reads OrcaSlicer's dialog answers and the file's notes with no guidance. Kenneth's words: treating the second model as if nothing happened is wrong.
- The shelved loader to port: branch `feature/project-skills-routing` (tip 77a8be964e; read `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/README.md` at commit 2d62184e37 for why it was shelved). Reuse: `AgentUI/src/skillParser.ts` (SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter, name rule, size checks) and `skills.ts` (glob-loads `skills/*/SKILL.md`), the `skills` bridge message with the host-side validation in that branch's `AgentHost.cpp` around line 973 (one message, sorted names, 16 KiB per text, 256 KiB payload, bridge error on a bad payload), and the `AgentSkill` record. Do not port: the `skill_read` tool, the skill index appended to the prompt, and any prompt text about choosing skills. The model never chooses.

## What to build

1. **Skill files on the page.** `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, frontmatter with `name`, a `trigger` the host understands (for this skill, a model arrived), and the body. Move the file-open text into `skills/model-arrived/SKILL.md` (name as you see fit, in a person's words). The body is the text the model gets; keep it as is except for the changes under 3. Keep `projectInstructions.ts` separate; it is the standing prompt and does not become a skill.
2. **The page sends all skills once per connection** with one `skills` message replacing `file_report_instructions`; the host stores them by trigger. Bridge version stays 1; list the capability as the printer and project instructions do (`protocol.json`, `AgentProtocol.hpp`, `protocol.ts`). The host refuses a bad payload with a bridge error and keeps the previous set. App-started turns that arrive before the skills, as today before `file_report_instructions`, wait the same way.
3. **The host adds the skill on the request where the load report first reaches the model**, for every source: the person's open or drop (today's Note path), and a `project_open` or `object_import_file` reply inside a turn, which is a continuation request built through `continue_after_tool` and `OpenAIResponsesAgent::continue_after_tool`; the skill goes in as a developer item after the tool outputs of that request. The text is never stored in the conversation document and appears on no later request. Two additions to the text: one sentence telling the model what the attached picture is, and one sentence, present only when no purpose is recorded for the conversation, saying that nothing is recorded about what this print is for and that the presets should be checked against the purpose once it is known. The skill text itself may say "the picture, when present"; the conditional sentence is added by the host, from state, in a fixed form so the same state gives the same bytes. The whole text deletes at least as much as it adds: the opening sentence "They have asked for nothing yet, so this message reports and offers, from the report alone" no longer holds for a tool import that fulfilled a request, so reword it for both cases.
4. **The picture.** Attach the active plate's iso render to that same request as an image input, using the offscreen render `view_render` already uses (`Workspace::render_view`, called from the coordinator about line 1288; images reach the model as `input_image` parts in `OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` lines about 219 and 278). Render when the request is built, not stored, so it is never replayed; none when the plate has no printable object. Widen `view_render`'s description (`ToolRegistry.cpp` about line 1151) so it also serves to tell what an object is when its name does not say, and regenerate `tests/project_prompt/project_tools.json` from the registry.
5. **The reminder line** on later requests (line 2115) stays as it is.

Never write "approve", "authorize", "confirm before" or "ask the user then call again" anywhere; tool-call approval was removed on 2026-10-07. Text the model reads lives on the page; text assembled from state lives in C++; say in the report which is which. The host must stay indifferent to the number of skills, since three more follow with other triggers.

## The eval

`tests/project_prompt` replays requests recorded from the app and asks the model for one step; each case names the sentence or skill it tests and never runs past its first response. Re-record `requests.json` with the shell harness's `--project-prompt-requests` (the recorder waits for OrcaSlicer's scheduled update, selects a per-conversation plate type, and points the version check at a closed port). Add two first-step cases that start at the request carrying the skill: the person opens a file whose name says nothing about what it is, expecting a reply that describes the object or asks what it is for and makes no change; and a tool import into an existing project, expecting the reply to report the import and make no further change. Make the recorder check that the skill and the picture are on exactly that request and absent from the next. Do not run a live model batch; put the proposed batch (cases, runs, estimated tokens) in the report instead. Credentials for a later run are in `~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`; never print them.

## Tests and build

`agent_bridge_tests` (cmake at `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake`, config RelWithDebInfo, or Release if disk is short; nohup long builds and watch the log; `cd` into your worktree in every Bash call), AgentUI vitest after `jusprin_web` is rebuilt, `workspace_contract_tests`, the shell harness default scenario, `python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`, `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only`. New behaviour gets a test that fails without the change: the skill on the three arrival paths and on no later request, the picture present and absent, the conditional sentence present and absent, the bad-payload refusal, the parser. Report line counts added and removed, and the skill text's byte count before and after.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

Branch `claude/project-prompt-harness` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/project-prompt-harness`), commit 70366449ae on jusprin-newui 336facf825. Not pushed. Baseline run 2026-10-15 at Kenneth's request (29df4b87f8): today's prompt 6b4b8b6188, 3 runs: 39/54 pass, 4 fail, 11 unobserved; 599,356 input tokens (459,776 cached), 9,784 output, 3 judge calls. The model often reads before replying, so first-person and reply-in-german observed no reply (0 pass, 3 unobserved each); answer-from-context 0/3 (calls workspace_inspect).

Design that differs from the 2026-10-15 handover, and why:
- Requests are recorded whole by a new shell harness mode, `--project-prompt-requests <script.json> <out.json>`: the project chat's real OpenAIResponsesAgent with a transport that holds each request; the scenario answers with scripted model outputs, so tools run for real and the app builds every request. `--manual-mcp` could not do it: in-turn tool results carry a `workspace` block (AgentHost::continue_after_tool, `context_json`) that MCP results never contain, and MCP rewrites stale errors to `stale_workspace` (in-app also says `stale_workspace` now).
- Case 16 uses the printer start G-code (22 KB) because presets_list pages at 25 (~1.5 KB) and every other read here stays under 4 KB: the 16 KiB omission note never fires for them.
- Cases 7/8 use initial_layer_print_height 0.5: a hand-typed layer_height above max_layer_height (0.28) is reset by an Orca dialog.
- Case 18's 3MF is written by the recorder (model_info->description + export_3mf); a PrusaSlicer 3MF loads geometry only and drops the description.

App problems found while recording (reported, not fixed): printer_setup_preview says valid/no mismatch for Bambu PETG HF on Smooth Cool Plate, then Orca refuses to slice; slice_start wait:true on that plate stays running (up to 15 min by the code) instead of failing.

**Why:** the next session runs Kenneth's batch or re-records after tool changes.
**How to apply:** re-record with the harness command in tests/project_prompt/README.md after tool/result changes; batch needs Kenneth's approval and the rewritten prompt. Related: [[project-prompt-harness-critique]], [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]], [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]].

**2026-10-15 later: Kenneth reversed the strict one-step rule for reads** (a9ffaf06e6): a read the case doesn't decide on is answered from real results the recorder captured at that point (workspace_inspect, slice_report, printer_list, settings_get of 32 keys for print + first object), max 3 per run; changes/judged calls still end the run. He wants flexibility, not exact-path expectations ("LMs are not deterministic"). First single run: 7 of 23 ended "no recorded answer" (settings_search, filament keys, legacy keys like fill_density, object_analyze, string targets) — answer coverage is the open weakness.

**Baseline with answered reads (f911bad664, 2026-10-15):** 23 cases x 3 on 6b4b8b6188, recording 80eddcbe9e (27 answers/point, requests.json ~4 MB): 47/69 pass, 8 fail, 14 unobserved; 1,256,920 input tokens (925,696 cached). Unobserved = string-JSON targets (app refuses), free-worded settings_search, object_analyze, unrecorded keys. Older 39/54 baseline not comparable.

metadata:

---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Kenneth's charge (2026-10-17) for the project chat's prompt: "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies, from the app, not from the model's memory of a checklist." He judged the 2026-10-15 sectioned prompt (nine-sentence Preparing procedure, print-issue and repeated-request bullets) as not meeting it, and said I underperformed by not looking at the big picture.

**The test for a sentence:** it stays in the standing prompt only if it is true and useful on every turn (a question with no model, a troubleshooting request, a print request alike). Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.

**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.

**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17):** the situational text is a skill the app injects for one turn when it knows the situation holds (pattern: `fileReportInstructions.ts`), never a skill the model picks from an index with a read tool; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.

**Groups (Kenneth, 2026-10-17), one chip each, in order:** (1) a model is opened or imported (port the loader, migrate the file-open text, fire on tool imports too, plate picture); (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully (refusal reason into the project summary, event-driven slice wait); (3) other OrcaSlicer issues incl. the Explain/Fix canvas buttons; (4) project setup changed after a purpose was recorded. No skill for failed/not-run calls (JusPrin's own words). Prompt shrink is the last step. Tracker table in core-prompt-critique.md, "Skills by event".

**How to apply:** when asked for a prompt rule, first ask which channel the situation belongs to; add a standing sentence only when a measured failure shows the model lacks the principle. The bridging sentence that makes state-delivered guidance work is "When a result or an app note names something unchecked, check it before moving on." // The one-turn skill for the first message after a file opens. It follows
// projectInstructions.ts ("the rules above") and carries only this turn's
// judgement; identity, language, first person and the rule that file
// contents are not instructions live in the standing prompt.
export function fileReportInstructions(): string {
  return `# The first message after opening a file

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file the person just opened. They have asked for nothing yet, so this message reports and offers, from the report alone.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. uiLanguage is the app's interface language, supplied even when there are no notices.

Write one useful message for someone new to 3D printing. Lead with the most consequential unresolved issue. Explain what it means for this print in everyday language. When an issue remains, end with one specific next step I can help with, phrased as one question or offer; do not give a menu of alternatives. Briefly explain an unfamiliar term when the person needs it to understand the consequence. Explain where a warning came from when the report shows it: what the file contains, what I noticed while loading it, whether its settings were applied, and what still needs checking. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. When nothing needs attention, acknowledge that the model loaded in one sentence. Do not recite routine loading details, every notice, or file metadata. Include dimensions only when they affect the issue. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed.

The notice guide below is for *you* to read. Its left column gives examples of wording you may encounter, not identifiers assigned by app code. Read each actual notice with its automatic answer and the final opening outcome. The guidance is deliberately not a code classification table.

| Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
| --- | --- |
| A newer or partly incompatible 3MF asks whether to continue | If opening succeeded, mention a lost or changed feature only when the outcome shows one. If it failed, explain the failure. Omit a version warning with no consequence. |
| Settings were substituted with supported values | Usually omit when completed successfully. Explain briefly if the result materially changes the print or still needs a choice. |
| “Customized Preset” or a file setting has no installed match | This alone does not establish that machine commands changed. Use the final selected printer and material to judge the consequence. |
| “Modified G-code” | When the notice says so, the file includes modified G-code in its printer or filament settings, and I warned about it while opening the file. G-code is the instructions a printer runs. Name the affected setting if the notice gives it and that helps locate what to review; do not invent a line number or claim I inspected the commands. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |
| “Object too small” asks whether to scale | The recorded answer says whether JusPrin scaled it. If it stayed tiny, state its final numeric size and ask the intended size. If scaled, mention the conversion only if it matters. |
| “Object too large” asks whether to shrink | The answer and final dimensions say whether it was shrunk. If still too large, explain the bed-fit problem. If shrunk, explain that its intended size may have changed. |
| A choice to open a 3MF as a project or geometry only | Use loadFacts.settingsOutcome to say whether the file's print settings were applied. Explain only when it changes the next step. |
| Connected-printer synchronization | Use the final selection and separately supplied connection state. Do not infer a connected machine from a preset name. |
| OBJ colour mapping, STEP mesh options, or unreadable STEP names | Mention a resulting colour, shape, precision or naming problem only when it matters to this model. |
| Multiple parts or files become one object | Mention grouping only if it changes how the person can print or edit the model. |
| A suggestion to simplify a very detailed model | Usually omit from the first message unless a current performance or editing problem exists. |
| A refusal to mix G-code with models, open multiple G-code files, or add models in preview mode | If the requested file did not open, explain that directly and give the next useful step. |
| “File contains no geometry” or a loading error | Lead with what failed and what, if anything, was added. Give the actual reason when available; do not invent one. |

An alarming notice does not override the final outcome. An automatic “No”, “Yes” or “OK” is JusPrin's action, not the person's preference. If several issues matter, address the most important decision first and briefly flag another consequential issue for later. If selectedSetupChange.printerPreset exists, name both its from and to selections in plain language, then ask which printer the person intends to use. If a tiny model was left unscaled, give its final size and ask the intended size. Do not turn an already completed change into a fresh action item.

Use useful file author advice only when it affects the next step; keep it secondary to an unresolved printer or size decision. Attribute it to the file.

Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Usually stay under 90 words. When no action is needed, stop without a question.`;
}

result.output:
# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge.

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it
is the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 17
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project

## Cases

Each case names the sentence of `projectInstructions.ts` it tests (line
numbers at 6b4b8b6188) in its docstring, and observes one step. "A change" is
any tool the registry does not mark read-only: applying settings, slicing,
printer setup, `intent_update`, `plan_set`, object edits, export. A run is a
pass, a fail, or unobserved: a step the case can say nothing about, most often
a read with no recorded answer. Unobserved runs are reported beside the
passes, never counted as either. Except where the table says a read decides
the case, a read is answered and the run goes on.

| Case | Point in the chat | Sentence | Pass | Fail |

| `advice-infill` | "what infill should I use for this?" | 14: advice calls for recommendations, not project changes | reply | a change |

| `after-slice` | after `slice_start` finished | 15, as above | `slice_report`, or a reply not claiming readiness (judged) | a readiness claim |
| `issue-fix` | canvas issue, "Help fix this issue." | 12: follow the requested scope | read or preview naming only `initial_layer_print_height` | a change or preview naming anything else |

- `petg-restated` and `petg-restated-after-read` were removed on 2026-10-16

  such as `"Cool Plate"`) has the person select that plate in the sidebar

  update, as a person typing would. Without it, the message after a
  `printer_setup` that switched the filament said the plate was still sliced

last reply, only where a string test cannot tell, for example, "set to 0.28"
from "could not set 0.28". Read the judge's reasons on failed runs before
trusting a count.

A new case is a class in `run_prompt_tests.py` with a `name`, a docstring
naming its sentence and a `check()`, a `record` for it in `script.json`, and a
new recording.

## Running it

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 51 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

To judge a prompt edit, run the earlier prompt with `--prompt-rev` and the
edit from the checkout on the same day, so both meet the same hosts.
Differences of a few runs are noise at three runs; run a case alone, with 20
runs, before reading a gap as real.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One step of the project chat against the live model, without the app.

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt (projectInstructions.ts), the
project tools and the chat. Each case here is one point in a project chat,
recorded from the real app, and the model's next step there, a tool call or a
reply, checked against one sentence of the prompt. A response may hold
several calls, and every one is judged: a change among them is the outcome
and ends the run, whatever came before it. A response of reads the case does
not decide on is answered, each read with the result the app gave for it at
the same point (recorded beside the request), and the model asked again, at
most MAX_READS times; nothing else is ever answered.

What the app sends, reproduced here:
  - instructions: rendered from projectInstructions.ts by
    tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs, so an edit to the prompt is tested
    without building anything;
  - tools: project_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the project chat
    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
  - input: everything else, as the app built it (requests.json). The shell
    harness's --project-prompt-requests mode plays script.json through the
    real app, with the model's outputs scripted and every tool run for real,
    and keeps the request at each point a case observes: the earlier turns as
    the app replays them, this turn's message with the workspace context, and
    this turn's calls with their live results. At the same point it calls
    the reads script.json's "answers" lists (workspace_inspect, slice_report,
    printer_list, object_analyze for each object, settings_get of every
    setting of the print, the first object, the filament and the printer,
    the filament's and printer's names asked under the print scope, a
    hand-kept list of other slicers' names, and settings_search for common
    queries) and keeps
    their results: those are the only answers a read can get.
The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs,
except which model answers them.

Usage:
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py
      [--runs N] [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--verbose] [--prompt-rev REV]
      [--model NAME [--endpoint URL] [--key-env NAME] [--provider HOST]...]
  tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only [--case NAME] [--runs N] [--prompt-rev REV]

--render-only sends nothing: it prints each case's full request body, one JSON
object per line, and on stderr the size of each and of the batch.

Prompt changes are evaluated on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to
the hosts tests/printer_prompt names (MODEL, PROVIDERS), and on nothing else.
The judge stays on OpenAI (OPENAI_API_KEY) whichever model answers.

Without --runs, the cases run share RUN_BUDGET runs: 3 each for 17 cases,
never more than MAX_RUNS for one case.

Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs (default:
all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's npm install
(src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RENDERER = HERE.parent / "printer_prompt" / "render_prompt.mjs"
# The model and hosts prompt changes are judged on, as tests/printer_prompt.
MODEL = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash"
ENDPOINT = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses"
KEY_ENV = "OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
PROVIDERS = ["Alibaba", "Novita", "Baidu", "AtlasCloud"]
JUDGE_ENDPOINT = "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses"
JUDGE_MODEL = "gpt-5.5-2026-04-23"  # pinned, so a count moves only when the prompt does
TOOLS = json.loads((HERE / "project_tools.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
_RECORDING = json.loads((HERE / "requests.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
REQUESTS = _RECORDING["cases"]
# The recorder keeps each distinct setting item once (settingItems), and the
# workspace block an answer shares with the others at its point once; both go
# back in exactly where the app put them.
for _request in REQUESTS.values():
    for _answer in _request["answers"]:
        _output = json.loads(_answer["output"])
        if _answer.pop("settingItems", False):
            for _field in ("items", "unknownKeys"):
                if _field in _output["result"]:
                    _output["result"][_field] = [_RECORDING["settingItems"][i] for i in _output["result"][_field]]
        if _answer.pop("sharedWorkspace", False):
            _output.update(_request["sharedWorkspace"])
        _answer["output"] = json.dumps(_output, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
MAX_READS = 3  # responses of reads answered in one run
RUN_BUDGET = 51
MAX_RUNS = 20
# ToolRegistry's ActionClass::ReadOnly tools. Every other tool changes the
# project, its plan or its printer setup, or slices: "a change" below.
READS = {"workspace_inspect", "settings_search", "settings_get", "settings_preview_patch", "presets_list", "printer_list",
         "printer_setup_preview", "slice_report", "slice_inspect", "view_render", "object_analyze",
         "object_divide_preview", "project_attachment_read"}
assert READS <= {tool["name"] for tool in TOOLS}

PASS, FAIL, UNOBSERVED, CONTINUE = "pass", "fail", "unobserved", "continue"
USAGE = {"requests": 0, "input_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "judge_requests": 0,
         "judge_input_tokens": 0, "judge_output_tokens": 0}
USAGE_LOCK = threading.Lock()


def render(revision=None):
    """The page's project prompt, from the checkout or from a git revision."""
    node = shutil.which("node")
    if node is None:
        sys.exit("node is required to render the project prompt")
    result = subprocess.run([node, str(RENDERER)] + ([revision] if revision else []), input='{"kind":"project"}',
                            capture_output=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
    return json.loads(result.stdout)["instructions"]


def post(body, key, endpoint=ENDPOINT):
    request = urllib.request.Request(endpoint, data=json.dumps(body).encode(), method="POST",
                                     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
                return json.load(response)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            # 403 is a spent key: stop, never retry or switch keys.
            if error.code not in (429, 500, 502, 503) or attempt == 4:
                raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {error.code}: {error.read().decode(errors='replace')[:500]}")
        except (urllib.error.URLError, ConnectionError):  # ConnectionError: a reset mid-response
            if attempt == 4:
                raise
        time.sleep(2 ** attempt)


def count(usage, judge=False):
    """Adds a response's token usage to the totals and logs it on stderr."""
    usage = usage or {}
    cached = (usage.get("input_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens", 0)
    with USAGE_LOCK:
        prefix = "judge_" if judge else ""
        USAGE[prefix + "requests"] += 1
        USAGE[prefix + "input_tokens"] += usage.get("input_tokens", 0)
        USAGE[prefix + "output_tokens"] += usage.get("output_tokens", 0)
        if not judge:
            USAGE["cached_tokens"] += cached
    print(f"usage{' judge' if judge else ''}: input {usage.get('input_tokens', 0)} (cached {cached}), "
          f"output {usage.get('output_tokens', 0)}", file=sys.stderr)


def dump(value):
    """JSON as the app writes it: compact, keys sorted."""
    return json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)


def output_text(item):
    return "".join(part.get("text", "") for part in item.get("content", []) if part.get("type") == "output_text")


def judge(log, question):
    """A yes or no about the conversation's last reply, from a stronger model,
    for what no string test can check. Returns (yes, why)."""
    schema = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["answer", "why"],
              "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}, "why": {"type": "string"}}}
    response = post({"model": JUDGE_MODEL, "store": False,
                     "instructions": "You read a chat between a 3D printing app's assistant and a person, and answer one "
                                     "question about it strictly as written, judging only what the messages say.",
                     "input": "\n".join(log) + "\n\nQuestion: " + question,
                     "text": {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "verdict", "strict": True, "schema": schema}}},
                    os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], JUDGE_ENDPOINT)
    count(response.get("usage"), judge=True)
    text = "".join(output_text(item) for item in response.get("output", []) if item.get("type") == "message")
    verdict = json.loads(text)
    return verdict["answer"] == "yes", verdict["why"]


def readable(item, limit=1500):
    """One input item as a line of the judge's transcript."""
    if item.get("type") == "function_call":
        return f"tool call: {item['name']} {item['arguments']}"
    if item.get("type") == "function_call_output":
        output = item["output"]
        return "tool result: " + (output if len(output) <= limit else output[:limit] + " …")
    if "role" not in item:
        return None  # a reasoning item: the model's own, not part of the chat
    content = item.get("content")
    # A user message's parts (the person's words, the app's <workspace> and
    # <print_issue> blocks, attachments) are separate in the request; keep
    # them apart here too.
    text = content if isinstance(content, str) else "\n\n".join(part["text"] for part in content or [] if "text" in part)
    return {"user": "person", "assistant": "assistant", "developer": "app"}.get(item["role"], item["role"]) + ": " + text


def last_result(request):
    """The result of the last tool call in a request, as the model reads it."""
    for item in reversed(request["body"]["input"]):
        if item.get("type") == "function_call_output":
            return json.loads(item["output"])

A skill contains things the model could do by itself if it had the right knowledge. It contains nothing that executes. Examples:

- judging evidence, such as telling an adhesion failure from wet filament in a photo;
- the order of a series of tool calls, and the reasons for that order. For "make it stronger": read the settings, change walls and infill, slice, read the report;
- facts about printing, such as what PETG tolerates;
- which question to ask when the answer would change the plan.

The file-load instructions (`AgentUI/src/fileReportInstructions.ts`) are a skill that the app inserts into the conversation for one turn. The first message after a file loads is a judgement about the load report. It is not an operation, so it is text. This is the only kind of skill built so far. The other kind would be a skill the model opens by name, after picking it from an index that has one line per skill. Nothing loads skills that way yet. Until something does, a skill is text that the app inserts on a turn where the app already knows the situation.

The cases in between:

- **A procedure made of existing tool calls.** It is a skill for as long as carrying it out takes judgement. It becomes a tool only when the steps are fixed and the person wants the whole thing as one action that can be undone. If there are many such fixed sequences, they go in one workflow registry (see [When resources or skills are appropriate](#when-resources-or-skills-are-appropriate)).
- **An analysis.** It is a tool when OrcaSlicer computes it and always gets the same answer, such as overhang angles from geometry. It is a skill when it is a judgement about evidence. Pair that skill with the tool that supplies the evidence (`view_render`, `slice_report`).
- **Large reference data.** When the model needs only one part of the data, make it a tool that returns the part an argument selects, as `settings_search` does. When the model needs to see all of the data before it can use any of it, make it text. The printer list described under [Input design](#input-design) is the case we measured: putting the whole list in the instructions worked better than the search tool.
- **A tool description versus a skill.** A tool description says when to call that one tool, in the words a person would use. A skill says how several tools fit together and what to conclude from their results. If a tool description has grown into a step-by-step procedure, move the procedure out into a skill.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about

# The "model arrived" skill: report

Branch `claude/skill-model-arrived`, two commits on local `jusprin-newui` 86f8395071 (not pushed, not merged):
bb148b0b9f (app and its tests) and 0f9ba01d33 (prompt eval). 86f8395071 replaced 46ee617812 on `jusprin-newui` this morning and contains its changes.

## 1. Problem

The project chat's guidance for "a model just arrived" (`fileReportInstructions.ts`) reached the model only when the person opened or dropped a file. When the model itself imported a model with a tool, the reply carried the same OrcaSlicer load report with no guidance, so the model read the dialog answers and the file's notes with nothing telling it how to treat them. There was also no general way for the app to add situational text ("skills") to a request. Three more skills are planned and need one.

## 2. What changed

**The loader.** Each skill is a file on the Agent page: `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Its frontmatter has `name` and `trigger`, and the body is the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection in one `skills` bridge message; this replaces `file_report_instructions`. The host stores the skills by trigger and knows nothing about how many there are. It refuses a bad payload with a bridge error and keeps the set it already had. The rules: one message, names sorted, one skill per trigger, at most 16 KiB of text per skill, at most 256 KiB in total. Project turns that the app starts before the skills arrive wait for them, the same way they wait for the project instructions. The bridge version stays 1, and the capability list gains `project_skills`. Nothing was ported from the old loader's model-picks-a-skill design: no `skill_read` tool, no skill index and no prompt text about choosing.

**The first skill.** `model-opened-or-imported` (trigger `model_arrived`) is the old file-open text, moved. The host adds it to the request where a load report first reaches the model:
- when the person opens or drops a file, on the request that starts the reply;
- when the model calls `object_import` (or `object_import_file`, or a `project_open` that fails), on the next request, after the tool results.

The skill is always the request's last item, with a picture of the active plate just before it. The picture is the offscreen iso render that `view_render` uses. It is drawn when the request is built, and only when the plate has a printable object. Neither the skill nor the picture is stored in the conversation. Neither appears on any later request, including the next request of the same turn.

**Changes to the text.**
- The opening sentence ("They have asked for nothing yet…") is rewritten so it covers both the person's open and a tool's import.
- One sentence now says what the picture is.
- Three sentences are gone: the `uiLanguage` sentence (a later sentence covers it), the "left column" sentence, and a duplicate of the tiny-model instruction already in the table.
- Size: the old text was 6,635 bytes; the new text is 6,525 bytes, or 6,624 bytes when the host's sentence is added.

**Where each piece of text lives.** All the model-read text is on the page (the skill). C++ supplies only state-based parts:
- the picture;
- the decision to fire the skill;
- one fixed sentence, added when the chat has no setup title and no answered intent field: "Nothing is recorded about what this print is for; once it is known, check the presets against it."

**Other changes.**
- `view_render`'s description now also offers the picture "to tell what an object is when its name does not say". `project_tools.json` was regenerated.
- The reminder line on later requests is unchanged.

**Lines changed.** App code: +376/−69. Tests and eval: +914/−76. The re-recorded `requests.json`: +9,349/−2,169.

## 3. Tests and results

All tests were run on the final build:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `agent_bridge_tests` | 303 cases pass, 12 of them new or extended |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest, after `jusprin_web` was rebuilt | 421 tests pass |
| Shell harness, default scenario | 553 checks, 0 failures |
| `test_steps.py` | 15 tests pass |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 19 cases render |

The new tests cover:
- the skill on the person's open, on `object_import` and on `object_import_file`, and on no later request;
- the picture, both present and absent;
- the purpose sentence, both present and absent, including an intent question that has no answer yet;
- refusal of a bad payload (14 kinds);
- the wait for the skills;
- the adapter dropping the skill and picture from the next request;
- the parser.

I checked that every new test fails when its behaviour is removed. I broke each behaviour on purpose in two C++ rounds, plus once in the parser and once in the runner, saw the matching tests fail, and restored the code.

**The eval.** `requests.json` was re-recorded with 0 failures. The 17 old points are identical apart from ids, timestamps and temporary paths. Two cases are new:
- `model-opened-unnamed`: the person imports `scan_0417.drc` (the Stanford bunny).
- `model-imported-by-tool`: the person attaches `part_7.drc` (the calicat), and `object_import` adds it.

The recorder checks that the skill and the picture are on exactly those two requests and absent from the next one. It saved both pictures, and I looked at them: they show the bunny and the cat.

## 4. Remaining issues

- **A `project_open` called by the model ends the turn.** Opening a project replaces the chat's document, which cancels the turn, so the result never reaches a model and the opened project's chat says nothing. I confirmed this in the real app: no request followed for two minutes. A test now holds this behaviour in place. Fixing it is your call. My recommendation: post the load report as a note in the opened project's chat and start a turn there, the same way a person's open works today.
- **The eval model cannot see pictures.** OpenRouter lists `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` as text only, and the app's default is `gpt-5.4-mini`. The two new cases may fail with a request error, or run without the picture.
- **The import picture hides one object.** `object_import` put the cat on top of the box (`object_analyze` reports them as overlapping), so the picture shows only the cat. That is how the import places objects today. The case does not ask the reply to mention the overlap.
- **Retrying a failed request after an import does not re-send the skill.**

**Proposed batch, not run.** The two new cases, 3 runs each: about 18 requests, roughly 200k–250k input tokens and 6 judge calls. Start with 1 run of each, to see whether OpenRouter accepts the picture for this model. If it refuses, choose between dropping the picture in the runner and running these two cases on an image model such as `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Optionally, run all 19 cases × 3 (about 950k input tokens) to check the `view_render` description change.

The "model arrived" skill is built and committed on `claude/skill-model-arrived`; nothing is pushed or merged. The app now adds the skill, with a picture of the plate, when the person opens or drops a file and when the model imports one with a tool. One path doesn't work: when the model itself calls `project_open`, the turn ends and the skill never reaches anyone. That needs your decision (below).

The branch has two commits on local `jusprin-newui` at 86f8395071. That commit replaced 46ee617812 this morning and contains its changes, which is why the branch is 16 commits ahead of origin, not 17:
- **bb148b0b9f** – the skill loader, the skill itself, the picture, and their tests.
- **0f9ba01d33** – the two new eval cases and a fresh `requests.json`.

The report is untracked at [skill-model-arrived-report.md](skill-model-arrived-report.md).

**What changed**
- **Skill files:** each skill is now `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, with a `name` and a `trigger` at the top and the model's text below. The page sends them all once per connection in a `skills` message, which replaces `file_report_instructions`.
- **Host:** it stores skills by trigger and works the same whatever their number. It refuses a bad payload with a bridge error and keeps the previous set, and turns the app starts wait until the skills arrive.
- **The skill and picture:** `model-opened-or-imported` is the old file-open text. It goes in as the last item of the request where the load report first reaches the model, with the plate picture just before it. Neither is stored, and neither appears on any later request, including the next one in the same turn.
- **The no-purpose sentence:** written in C++ and added only when the chat has no purpose recorded. It is the only text the model reads that doesn't live on the page.
- **Size:** the skill text went from 6,635 to 6,525 bytes, or 6,624 with the sentence added.
- **Lines:** app code +376/−69, tests and eval +914/−76, plus the re-recorded `requests.json`.

**Tests**
- Everything passes on the final build: `agent_bridge_tests` (303 cases), `workspace_contract_tests` (42), AgentUI vitest after rebuilding `jusprin_web` (421), the shell harness default scenario (553 checks, 0 failures), `test_steps.py` (15), and `--render-only` (19 cases).
- I removed each new behaviour on purpose and confirmed its test fails, then restored the code.
- The 17 existing eval points are unchanged apart from ids, timestamps and temp paths.
- The two new cases record the skill and picture on exactly the right request, and both are gone from the next one. I looked at the recorded pictures: they show the bunny and the cat.

**Three things you'll want to know**
1. **The tool-import case uses an attached file.** In the project chat, `object_import_file` is only offered to outside MCP clients. The chat's own import is `object_import`, which imports a file the person attached, so that's what the case uses.
2. **`project_open` called by the model ends the turn.** Opening a project replaces the chat's document, which cancels the turn, so the result never reaches the model. I confirmed this in the real app, and a test now holds that behaviour in place. Fixing it is your call. I'd post the load report as a note in the newly opened project's chat and start a turn there, the same way a person's open works today.
3. **The eval model can't see pictures.** OpenRouter lists `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` as text-only; the app's own default model is `gpt-5.4-mini`. The two new cases may fail with a request error or run without the picture.

**Proposed live batch (not run):** the two new cases, 3 runs each, about 18 requests and roughly 200k–250k input tokens, with 6 judge calls. I'd start with one run of each to see whether OpenRouter accepts the picture. If it doesn't, the choice is between dropping the picture in the eval runner and running these two cases on an image-capable model such as `deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Optionally, a full run of all 19 cases (about 950k input tokens) would check the change to the `view_render` description.

I won't make changes until you say go. Here is my understanding and what I'll do.

**What went wrong.** You asked that every new model arriving in the in-app chat gets the skill, with only MCP clients excluded. I treated the AI's `project_open` as an existing gap, wrote a test that keeps it broken, and called the fix your decision. That was wrong. Without that path the task doesn't meet its goal, because opening a file as a new project is a main way the AI brings in a model.

**Why `project_open` loses the skill.** I've now read the code; this isn't a guess:
- Opening a project swaps in the new project's conversation document. That cancels the running turn and drops its pending tool results (`AgentHost::on_document_replaced`).
- Then the tool-activity listener in `AgentHost.cpp` (around line 671) discards any finished call that belongs to the project just closed. The `project_open` result, with OrcaSlicer's load report inside it, is thrown away there.
- The workspace adapter sends a person's load report to `on_file_loaded`. It does not do that for loads the AI starts. So the opened project's chat never hears about the file at all.

**What I'll do, on the same branch:**
1. **Hand the report to the new chat.** In that listener, just before the result is discarded, I'll check for a `project_open` that succeeded, came from the in-app AI (`ToolSource::Agent`, not `ToolSource::Mcp`), and carries a load report. If so, I'll post the file-load note in the newly opened project's chat and start a turn there. I'll reuse the code `on_file_loaded` runs for your own opens, so the skill and the plate picture come along the same way.
2. **Keep your rule about existing projects.** That code already skips a reopened project that has a conversation, unless OrcaSlicer said something while loading. The AI choosing "continue the existing project" goes through the same check, so it stays silent.
3. **Leave the existing paths as they are:**
   - your own open, drop or import: skill on the request that starts the reply;
   - the AI's `object_import` and a `project_open` that fails: skill after the tool results;
   - MCP clients: never.
4. **Check the picture timing in the real app.** The new turn would start right after the load finishes. I'll look at the recorded picture to confirm it shows the opened model and not an empty or stale plate. If the canvas isn't ready yet, I'll start the turn one event-loop step later, the same way your own opens are delivered.
5. **Tests:**
   - Flip the native test that currently holds the broken behaviour. It will check that the opened project's chat gets the note, a turn, the skill and the picture.
   - Add a test that an MCP client's `project_open` produces none of that.
   - Add a test that reopening an existing project with its conversation produces none of that.
   - Break each new behaviour on purpose and confirm its test fails.
6. **Eval:** add a recorder case where the AI opens a file as a new project. The recorder will check that the skill and picture are on the first request in the new project's chat, and on nothing after it.
7. **Wrap up:** rerun the full test set, re-record `requests.json`, commit, and correct the report. The report will note that `object_import` replaced the `object_import_file` you specified, and why.

**What changes for you:** your request ("open bracket.stl") stays in the old project's chat. The new project's chat starts with the file note and the AI's first message about the file, the same as when you open a file yourself.

**Still waiting on your decision:** the eval model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, takes text only, so it can't see the plate picture. No live batch runs until you choose between dropping the picture in the eval runner and running those cases on a model that takes images.

**The skills mechanism**
- **Two kinds of skill, one loader.** Every skill stays a `SKILL.md` on the page.

  - A discretionary skill has a `description`, and the model can read it whenever it judges it useful.

**`project_open` called by the AI**
1. The current turn is interrupted. That already happens when the project is swapped.
2. Opening an internal project does nothing.
3. Otherwise, the events and dialogs OrcaSlicer produces during the open are gathered by the existing load-report collection in the workspace adapter. The same collector already gathers them for the AI's open, so I'll move code rather than write new.
4. The collected report is handed to the opened project's new chat, through exactly the path your own opens take today: the file note, then a turn with the model-arrived skill.
5. One mechanism, nothing kept alongside. I read "the hard-coded one-off" as the old special-cased file-report instructions, which are already gone. I'll also check what else in that path is still special-cased (see question 4).

**Changes to the skill text**

- Ask the person whether the AI should look at the model to guess what it's for, the intent, and the slicing strategy.

"Ask whether to look at the model" suggests no picture until the person says yes, after which the AI calls `view_render`. Should I remove the automatic picture? I recommend removing it. Otherwise the question asks permission for something the model has already seen.

   - In `skill_read`'s description (my recommendation): the standing prompt stays principles-only.
   - In the system prompt, as Claude Code does.

   - the reminder line on later requests ("Earlier file-load reports… are source data");
   - the fixed "Nothing is recorded about what this print is for" sentence.

   Once the skill checks presets, that sentence mostly repeats it, so I'd delete it. Should the reminder line also move into a skill? The original brief said to keep it as it is.

**Limits the new text runs into.** The skill currently says to end with one question or offer and to stay under 90 words. The presets suggestion plus the "may I look?" question push against both. I'll have it lead with whichever matters more and allow the second. The text will also grow, so the original "delete at least as much as you add" rule no longer holds.

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the model that just arrived, opened by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what arrived and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

# The "model arrived" skill: report

The branch is `claude/skill-model-arrived`. It has four commits on top of local `jusprin-newui` 86f8395071 and is neither pushed nor merged:
- bb148b0b9f – the skill loader and the skill, with their tests
- 0f9ba01d33 – the prompt eval cases and a new recording
- 5d790d603f – the project_open hand-off, `skill_read`, and the revised skill text
- 0094812092 – the project_open eval case and a new recording

86f8395071 replaced 46ee617812 on `jusprin-newui` on 2026-10-17, and contains its changes.

## 1. Problem

The project chat had one piece of situational guidance: what to say when a model arrives. It reached the model only when the person opened or dropped a file. It did not reach the model in two cases:
- **The AI imports a model** in the middle of a turn. The tool's reply carried OrcaSlicer's load report, but no guidance.
- **The AI opens a model with `project_open`.** Opening a project replaces the chat's document with the new project's, which ends the turn. The report reached no model, and the opened project's chat said nothing at all.

There was also no general way for the app to add situational text, called "skills", to a request.

## 2. What changed

**Skills on the page.** Each skill is a file on the Agent page: `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The frontmatter (the header at the top of the file) holds the skill's `name`, plus a `trigger`, a `description`, or both. The body is the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection in one `skills` bridge message, which replaces `file_report_instructions`.

The app refuses a bad message with a bridge error and keeps the skills it already had. The rules are:
- names sorted, at most one skill per trigger;
- each description one line of at most 300 bytes;
- each skill's text at most 16 KiB, and at most 256 KiB for the whole message.

The bridge version stays 1; the capability list gains `project_skills`. A project turn that the app starts before the skills arrive waits for them.

**Two kinds of skill.**
- **A skill with a trigger belongs to the app.** When its event happens, the app adds the skill as the last item of the one request where the model first reads about that event. It is never stored in the conversation, and it appears on no later request, including the next request of the same turn.
- **A skill with a description belongs to the model.** The model reads it with `skill_read`, which is ported from the suspended skills branch. `skill_read` lists the described skills in its own tool description and reads only those. It is offered only while at least one such skill exists. None exists yet, so no request carries `skill_read` today.

**The first skill.** `model-opened-or-imported` (trigger `model_arrived`) is the old file-open text, moved into a skill file. It goes out with a picture of the active plate placed just before it. The picture is the offscreen iso view that `view_render` uses, drawn when the request is built. It fires in four situations:

| What happened | Where the skill goes |
|---|---|
| The person opens or drops a file | On the request that starts the reply |
| The AI runs `object_import`, or a `project_open` that fails | After the tool results, in the same turn |
| The AI's `project_open` succeeds | In the opened project's chat: the app posts the load report there and starts a turn, the same path the person's own open takes |
| An MCP client opens or imports anything | Never |

When an existing project is reopened with its conversation, the app speaks only if OrcaSlicer said something while loading it, as before. When the AI continues an earlier project, nothing is loaded, so nothing is said.

**Skill text.** The skill now tells the model to:
- look at the attached picture and guess what the object is, what it is for, and how to slice it;
- check the selected presets and plate type against that guess and against the available presets, and suggest a better one without changing it;
- end with its best guess at what the person wants next, in whatever form fits.

The old "one question or offer, under 90 words" rule is gone. The text grew from 6,635 to 6,918 bytes.

**Where the text lives.** Everything the model reads is on the page. C++ supplies only things built from the app's state:
- the picture;
- the decision to fire a skill;
- the list of skill names and descriptions in `skill_read`'s description;
- one fixed sentence when no purpose is recorded for the print.

**Also changed.**
- `view_render`'s description now also says it can tell what an object is.
- `project_tools.json` was regenerated.

**Size.** App code: +507/−83 lines. Tests and eval: +1,164/−77 lines. `requests.json`: +11,952/−2,169 lines.

## 3. Tests and results

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `agent_bridge_tests` | 310 cases pass |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest, after `jusprin_web` was rebuilt | 421 tests pass |
| Shell harness, default scenario | 0 failures |
| `test_steps.py` | 15 tests pass |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 20 cases render |

The new tests cover:
- the three ways a model can arrive inside the app: your own open, the AI's import, and the AI's open;
- MCP opens, which stay silent;
- continuing an earlier project;
- the skill and picture appearing on no later request;
- the picture and the purpose sentence, each both present and absent;
- `skill_read`: when it is offered, what it may read, and its arguments;
- bad skills messages being refused;
- the parser.

I broke each behaviour on purpose and saw its test fail.

**Real app.** The AI's `project_open` now produces a request in the opened project's chat. That request holds only the report, the picture and the skill, with none of the old chat's history. The picture shows the opened model.

**Eval recording.** `requests.json` was recorded again with 0 failures. Only the skill text changed on the earlier points; other differences are ids, timestamps and temporary paths. There are three skill cases: `model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool` and `model-opened-by-tool`. The recorder checks that the skill and picture sit on exactly the right request and are gone from the next one.

## 4. Remaining issues

- **No live batch was run** (you'll test it). The eval model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, is listed by OpenRouter as text-only, so it may refuse the picture or run without it.
- **The original brief named `object_import_file`, which the in-app chat cannot call.** It is offered only to MCP clients. The eval case uses `object_import` instead, which imports a file the person attached to their message.
- **`object_import` placed the cat on top of the existing box,** so the picture hides the box. That is how imports are placed today; this change didn't cause it.
- **Two small effects of the AI's `project_open`:**
  - The person's request ("open part_9.drc") stays in the old project's chat.
  - Retrying a failed request after an import does not re-send the skill.
